newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: LUKoil says to buy five pct Tengiz stake.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil says to buy five pct Tengiz stake.

text.p: Russia's largest oil company NK LUKoil is near final agreement with Chevron Corp to buy a five percent stake from the U.S. oil major in its Tengiz oil project in Kazakhstan, LUKoil president Vagit Alekperov said on Tuesday.

"Today we came close to reaching a final agreement with Chevron and we hope within a week to sign a contract to buy five percent of their (total) stake in Tengiz," Alekperov told reporters in the Moldovan capital Chisinau.
Alekperov also said LUKoil hoped to sign an agreement, possibly in February, with Baghdad to revive a stalled billion-dollar project to develop oil reserves in Iraq's Western Kurna oilfield.
"Our 1997 programme envisages bringing on line the giant Western Kurna deposit in Iraq," he said. "We hope to sign a contract in February."

Chevron owns a 50 percent stake in the $20 billion joint TengizChevroil (TCO) venture to develop Tengiz, which plans to increase its output to at least 180,000 barrels per day by the end of this year.
Mobil Corp of the United States has a 25 percent stake in TCO, while the Kazakh government owns the rest.
LUKoil holds a 70 percent stake in a stalled production-sharing deal with two Russian firms, Zarubezhneft and Mashinoimport, to develop Iraq's Western Kurna and Northern Rumeila fields.
One of the Russian partners had completed the first stage of investments in the project before the United Nations slapped on sanctions after the 1991 Gulf War.
U.S. oil company Atlantic Richfield (ARCO) said in October 1996 that it was likely to get involved in Tengiz through its alliance with LUKoil.
ARCO and LUKoil have an agreement to spend $3 billion on joint ventures in Russia and overseas, with most of the financing to come from ARCO.
ARCO owns about eight percent of LUKoil's total equity.
Tengiz has estimated crude oil reserves of six to nine billion barrels.
